title: DIY Garlic‑Infused Candle Using a Garlic Press for Aroma
meta_description: Learn how to make a savory, aroma-boosting garlic candle using a garlic press DIY garlic candle method. Perfect for kitchen scenting and DIY gifts!
html:
Most people think of candles as smelling like vanilla or lavender, but if you're a true foodie, you know that the pungent, savory scent of garlic is the heart of a cozy kitchen. While you wouldn't want your bedroom smelling like a bistro, a garlic-infused candle is a fantastic way to lean into a savory aesthetic or create a unique, aromatic gift for a fellow home cook.

The secret to a potent scent is maximizing the release of allicin—the compound that gives garlic its signature punch. That is where a garlic press DIY garlic candle approach comes in. By using a high-quality Garlic Press to crush the cloves rather than slicing them, you rupture more cell walls, ensuring the oil is concentrated and the aroma is intense.

Why Use a Garlic Press for Your Candle?

When making infused products, the goal is surface area. Slicing garlic with a knife leaves many of the aromatic oils trapped inside the clove. When you use a Garlic Press, you are essentially forcing the garlic through a grid of small holes, creating a paste that blends more seamlessly into the wax and carrier oils.

Our favorite Garlic Press—the one featuring sturdy stainless steel and silicone components—is ideal for this because it handles the pressure of multiple cloves without bending. Plus, the silicone parts make it easy to pop out the garlic paste so you can transfer it directly into your melting pot without waste.

Materials You Will Need

Before you start, gather your supplies. You'll want materials that can handle heat and won't interfere with the scent profiles.

  • 1 cup soy wax flakes (soy holds scent better than paraffin)
  • 1/4 cup carrier oil (sweet almond or olive oil works best)
  • 4-6 large cloves of fresh garlic
  • Cotton candle wick and a glass jar
  • A double boiler or heat-proof bowl over a pot of simmering water
  • A sturdy Garlic Press for processing the cloves

Step-by-Step Garlic Press DIY Garlic Candle Instructions

Follow these steps to ensure your candle smells like a gourmet kitchen rather than burnt toast. The key is temperature control; if you overheat the garlic, you'll lose the fresh aroma.

1. Prepare the Garlic Paste: Peel your cloves and run them through your Garlic Press. Squeeze fresh garlic in seconds to create a fine, consistent paste. The more uniform the paste, the better it will integrate with the wax.

2. Create the Garlic-Oil Infusion: Place your carrier oil and the pressed garlic paste in your double boiler. Heat on low for about 15-20 minutes. Do not let the oil boil, as this will scorch the garlic and ruin the scent. You want a gentle steep that pulls the aromatics into the oil.

3. Melt the Wax: In a separate container or after straining the garlic solids from the oil, add your soy wax flakes. Stir gently until the wax is completely liquid and combined with the infused oil.

4. Set the Wick: While the wax cools slightly, secure your wick to the bottom of the glass jar using a drop of melted wax or a wick sticker.

5. The Final Pour: Pour the garlic-infused wax into the jar. Let it sit undisturbed for 24 hours to cure. This allows the scent molecules to bond with the wax crystals for a longer-lasting aroma.

Tips for the Best Savory Scent

If you find the scent of pure garlic too aggressive, you can customize your blend. Adding a pinch of dried rosemary or a few drops of thyme essential oil to the wax mixture creates a "Roasted Garlic and Herbs" profile that feels more like a candle and less like a condiment.

To keep your workspace clean, remember that the Garlic Press you use should be cleaned immediately after the process. Since our recommended Garlic Press is designed to clean up easy, you can simply rinse the stainless steel and silicone parts under warm water to remove any sticky residue.

Safety and Usage Notes

Because this candle contains organic matter (garlic oil), always burn it on a heat-resistant coaster. Keep the flame trimmed to 1/4 inch to prevent soot. This candle is intended for aroma and decorative purposes; while the ingredients are food-grade, the wax is not edible!

This project is a great way to repurpose a kitchen tool for a craft project. Using a Garlic Press for tasks beyond just cooking shows just how versatile a sturdy, well-made tool can be in the home.

FAQ

Will the candle smell like actual food?

Yes, it will have a savory, pungent aroma. Because we use a Garlic Press to maximize the oil release, the scent is quite realistic. It's perfect for neutralizing strong odors in the kitchen after cooking fish or onions.

Can I use garlic powder instead of fresh cloves?

You can, but the result won't be as potent. Fresh garlic contains volatile oils that powder lacks. To get that "fresh-pressed" scent, using a Garlic Press with fresh cloves is the only way to go.

How long does a DIY garlic candle last?

Depending on the size of your jar, a soy-based garlic candle typically lasts 20-30 hours. Store it in a cool, dry place when not in use to preserve the aromatic oils.
